messages:
elaine: Heads up — charts on the metrics dashboard are stalling on initial paint after this morning's telemetry client rollout (canary). Frames drop for ~400–600ms on first load. https://console.redwood.local/dash/heatmap shows it clearly :frowning_face:

jorge: Seen it too. Safari and Chrome both. CPU spikes on main thread when the page loads the telemetry payload.

ken: any errors in console? stack traces?

elaine: Console shows big parse of a single 1.2MB telemetry blob, then repeated GC. quick snippet:```
telemetry-client.js: parseTelemetry(…)
  at telemetry-client.js:432:12
Uncaught (in promise) RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
```

samir: That 1.2MB blob is from the new sampling payload — we started including full-event-context for trace correlation (commit a1f3b2c) and it's exploding client-side.

alisha: Deploy-bot says canary finished at 1716499800 with tag telemetry/v2-canary.

deploy-bot: canary deployment telemetry/v2-canary completed on 10% of traffic (region: us-west).

elaine: Workaround for now: if someone can flip the canary to 0 or rollback that commit, dashboards are unusable for a subset of users. Alternative: lazy-load chart library until after parsing.

jorge: I can flip the canary to 0. Before we do that, can we try reducing payload size client-side? Maybe only send the reduced context for non-enterprise users.

ken: Two immediate options: 1) rollback telemetry/v2-canary, 2) ship a tiny client-side patch that streams parse via TextDecoder/worker. Both are doable, but streaming into a worker is safer long-term.

samir: We should also consider server-side change: gate the full-event-context behind route-level quota. Sending full context for every metric read was an RPC change — we can restrict to sampled routes. Something like:```json
{"route_quota":{
  "/dash/*": {"telemetryFull": 0.05},
  "/api/*": {"telemetryFull": 0.2}
}}
```

alisha: +1 for route quota. Ops wants a conservative rollout though — can't flip quotas globally without a rollback plan.

elaine: I rolled canary to 0 at 1716500100 — confirm if dashboards recover.

jorge: Confirmed metrics dashboard responsiveness back to expected baseline on my machine. No more main-thread spike. :thumbsup:

samir: Filed a quick follow-up: we need a telemetry policy (who gets full context, sampling rates per tenant, and a server-side limiter). I'll open an RFC.

ken: For the console frontend fix, I'll prototype worker-based parse + async chart import. If perf looks good we'll land a patch behind a feature flag and then revert server change gradually.

elaine: Thanks. Action items: samir RFC for telemetry policy, ken implement worker parse + lazy chart import, ops keep canary at 0 until we have a staged plan.

alisha: Noted — I'll update the rollout doc and alert SRE on potential user-facing errors while we test.

deploy-bot: rollback action executed: telemetry/v2-canary -> 0% at 1716500100 (initiated by elaine).

elaine: Filing postmortem notes in #postmortems later today. If anyone saw persistent client-side cache corruption after the rollback, ping me.

jorge: small ask — can we add a console metric for 'telemetry parse time' so we detect this earlier on canaries next time?

samir: Good call. I'll add a perf counter in the telemetry ingestion path and dashboard tile for the next sprint.

elaine: OK closing this thread unless new regressions show up. Thanks all.
